title: Degrees of Separation
real_world_story: In a social network, measuring how closely two members are connected is critical for recommendation relevance and privacy settings. Each direct friendship represents 1 connection hop. If two users are not directly connected but share a mutual friend, they are separated by 2 hops. The platform must compute the minimum number of friendship hops between any two members.
problem_statement: Given an unweighted social network graph of N users numbered 1 to N and M bidirectional friendships, determine the minimum number of friendship hops needed to connect a source user S and a destination user D. If S and D are the same user, the distance is 0. If no sequence of friendships connects S and D, return -1.
task: Read the graph description and query pair (S, D), then print the minimum friendship distance from S to D, or -1 if unreachable.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and M, denoting the number of users and friendships.
The next M lines each contain two space-separated integers u and v (1 <= u, v <= N), representing an undirected friendship between user u and user v.
The final line contains two space-separated integers S and D, representing the source and destination user IDs.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the minimum number of friendship hops from user S to user D, or -1 if no path exists.

examples.explanation: The shortest path from user 1 to user 4 is 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, which consists of 3 friendship hops.
User 4 is completely disconnected from user 1. No friendship chain exists, so output -1.
The source user and destination user are identical (user 2), requiring 0 hops.

real_world_takeaway: Breadth-First Search on an unweighted graph explores layer-by-layer, guaranteeing that the first time a destination is reached, the path taken has the minimal number of hops.
